question: The author of Prayag Prashasti, Harisena, was the court poet of whom among the following Gupta rulers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harisena was a renowned poet and scholar in the court of the Gupta emperor **Samudragupta**.
 
• The Prayag Prashasti, also known as the **Allahabad Pillar Inscription**, was composed by Harisena.
 
• The inscription is an important source of historical information about the reign and accomplishments of Samudragupta.
 
• It provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's military campaigns, conquests, and his skills as a ruler and administrator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prayag Prashasti**

 
 
• The Prayag Prashasti is an inscription found on the Allahabad Pillar, which was originally erected by Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, and later inscribed by Samudragupta.
 
• It is written in classical Sanskrit and is composed in the form of a eulogy or prashasti.
 
• The inscription highlights Samudragupta's victories over various kings and his establishment of a vast empire.
 
• It also mentions his patronage of arts and culture, portraying him as a versatile and benevolent ruler.
 
 
 
• **Samudragupta**
 
 
• Samudragupta was one of the greatest rulers of the Gupta Empire, often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" for his extensive military campaigns and conquests.
 
• He ruled from approximately 335 to 375 CE and was known for his administrative skills, cultural patronage, and military prowess.
 
• His reign marked a golden age of art, literature, and science in ancient India.
 
• Samudragupta's achievements are celebrated in various historical records and inscriptions, with the Prayag Prashasti being one of the most significant.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, which lasted from around 320 to 550 CE, is considered a classical period in Indian history, known for its advancements in arts, science, and political administration.
 
• It was established by Sri Gupta and reached its zenith under rulers like Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
 
• The period saw the flourishing of classical Sanskrit literature, significant developments in mathematics and astronomy, and the creation of magnificent art and architecture.
 
• The decline of the Gupta Empire began in the late 5th century, eventually leading to its fall due to invasions and internal conflicts.
